inherited_limitations.topic: `fence_from_json` accepts `"format": true` as version 1, because `True == 1` in Python.
inherited_limitations.status: reproduced faithfully; candidate for repair as an INTENTIONAL DIVERGENCE now that D-0023 has superseded D-0022
inherited_limitations.detail: `state.py` checks `payload.get("format") != FENCE_FORMAT_VERSION`, and `bool` is a subclass of `int` in Python, so a persisted fence whose `"format"` is the JSON literal `true` passes interlock's version check and is loaded. `true !== 1` in JavaScript, so reproducing it took an explicit boolean branch -- `equalsFormatVersion` in src/fencing/state.ts, which maps `true` to 1 and `false` to 0 and is commented as the inherited defect it is. (`1.0 == 1` needs no branch: JSON.parse collapses both spellings to one `number`.) The behaviour is pinned by `test_an_unknown_format_version_is_rejected` only in the negative direction -- that case feeds `2`, not `true` -- so no ported case would turn red if the branch were removed. Under the policy that replaced D-0022 (interlock is frozen; inherited defects are repaired in continuo and recorded here as intentional divergences with continuo authoritative) this is a repair candidate, and the repair is one line: delete the boolean branch so a `"format": true` fence is rejected as malformed, which is fail-closed and strictly the safer direction. It is NOT done in this PR because this PR's job is to establish the translated baseline, and a divergence introduced in the same commit that first records the behaviour leaves nothing to compare against. The repair belongs in the NEXT PR of this lane that touches src/fencing/state.ts (PR 3, readback), which must flip this entry to an intentional divergence, add a target-only case feeding `true` and expecting a refusal, and say so in its PR body.
